title: Release audit: Redaction misses values separated from a secret label by a newline and values be
summary: Treat all whitespace including line breaks as separators between label, separator and value, and do not reject the first value character after an explicit colon or equals. Add direct and session-level tests for newline-separated and punctuation-prefixed values.
requirements: When a secret label is separated from its value by whitespace that contains a line break instead of, or in addition to, spaces and tabs, the value is masked and the label, the separator and the line break stay visible.
The line-break rule applies whether the label and the value reach the owner as one block of text or are displayed on separate lines.

After an explicit colon or equals separator, a value that begins with punctuation is masked: the label, the separator and the space before the value stay visible and exactly one marker takes the place of the punctuation and the value.
A bracketed value after an explicit colon or equals separator is masked so that no character of the value remains visible and exactly one marker appears.
Quotation characters that enclose a value keep the behaviour they already have: the quotation characters stay visible and the marker stands between them.
Repeated separator characters stay visible and only the value is replaced.
Each masked value carries exactly one marker, and masking an already masked text changes nothing.
No character of a masked value appears anywhere in the text the client shows, for every form this task adds and every form it already handled.
A mention of a secret label that carries no value, on one line or followed by a line break, stays exactly as written.
Text without a secret value stays exactly as written, character for character, including its line breaks.
Every masking form the client already handles keeps its current rendering.
acceptance: A label, an explicit colon and a line break followed by a value on the next line are shown as the label, the colon, the same line break and one marker, and no character of the value is visible.
A label, a line break and a value on the next line without any separator are shown as the label, the same line break and one marker, and no character of the value is visible.
A text in which only one line carries the value keeps its line count and every other line character for character, while the value line shows one marker in place of the value.
A value introduced by an exclamation mark after an explicit colon or equals separator loses the exclamation mark and the value and gains exactly one marker; no character of the value is visible.
A value enclosed in square brackets after an explicit colon or equals separator loses the brackets and the value and gains exactly one marker; no character of the value is visible.
A quoted value after a label renders exactly as it renders today, with the quotation characters visible and one marker between them.
An authorization scheme word before a credential stays visible and the credential is replaced by one marker, as today.
A label that carries no value is unchanged, both on a single line and when a line break follows the label.
Secret-free text, including text with punctuation, line breaks and several lines, is returned unchanged.
For every form this task adds, masking twice gives the same text as masking once and the text contains exactly one marker per masked value.
The whole existing expectation suite passes.
The finding is resolved for any secret label, any explicit separator and any punctuation, not only for the examples named in the audit finding.
plan_goal: Forgel Code: interactive agent client instead of a command wrapper

result.summary:
Widened the client-side masking in forgel_code/interactive.py so that a secret value is hidden however it is separated from its label. The gap was two-fold: the separator gap only accepted spaces and tabs, and the value after an explicit ':' or '=' separator could only be a word-like run, so a value on the next line or a value introduced by punctuation reached the screen.

Changes:
- The gap between a label and its value (and between a value and an authorization scheme word) is now skipped with a single whitespace predicate that includes line breaks and the other whitespace characters, so `password:\nhunter2`, `password\nhunter2`, `token =\r\nabc123` and `Authorization:\nBearer abc123` are masked while every separator character and the line break stay visible.
- After an explicit ':'/'=' separator a separate value-span helper is used: quotation marks keep their current enclosing rendering, a word-like value keeps the existing rendering, and any other punctuation that introduces a value is treated as part of the value, so `password: !hunter2` becomes `password: [redacted]` and a bracketed run `password: [hunter2]` is hidden whole with one marker.
- Repeated separators, prose/mention/copula/authorization-scheme exceptions and the masker's own marker stay untouched, so existing renderings and idempotence are preserved.

Tests: extended tests/test_redact.py with a new `LineBreakAndPunctuationFormTest` class (line-break separation with and without a separator, CRLF and mixed whitespace, line count and other lines unchanged, punctuation-prefixed values across labels, bracketed values, valueless labels, secret-free multiline text, idempotence and one marker per masked value) plus a screen test that a multiline engine reply with a value on the next line and a punctuation-prefixed value shows no secret characters. The full suite passes: `python -m pytest -q` → 308 passed, 293 subtests passed.
assumptions: A run of any whitespace that contains a line break (or only spacing) separates a label from its value, mirroring the existing space-and-tab rule; carriage returns are included so CRLF text is masked.

Punctuation directly before a value after an explicit ':'/'=' separator is treated as part of the value and replaced together with it, while enclosing quotation characters keep their visible rendering; trailing clause punctuation after the value stays visible as before.
A bracketed run after an explicit separator is hidden whole, brackets included, on the value's own line; a '[' that opens no such run keeps its previous treatment.
The existing mention, prose-word, copula and authorization-scheme rules keep precedence over the widened gap rule, so ordinary prose across a line break is not masked.
No documentation or changelog update was made, following the task's non-goals.

checks.criterion: A label, an explicit colon and a line break followed by a value on the next line are shown as the label, the colon, the same line break and one marker, and no character of the value is visible.
The finding is resolved for any secret label, any explicit separator and any punctuation, not only for the examples named in the audit finding.

review.summary: The attributed change is coherent and complete: `forgel_code/interactive.py` widens the label/value gap to whitespace containing line breaks, keeps every separator and line break visible, and adds a punctuation/bracket-aware value span for explicit ':'/'=' separators together with an idempotence guard for the marker. `tests/test_redact.py` adds focused unit tests for the newline, CRLF, punctuation-prefixed, bracketed, no-value, secret-free and double-masking forms plus a session-level test that the client masks a value on the line after its label in an engine reply, without removing or weakening any existing expectation. The change sticks to the requested scope (no new configuration, no label/scheme changes, no engine interface changes, no documentation), contains no unrelated or generated files, and the deterministic checks reported by QA pass.

requirements.requirement: FR-1 / AC-1: label + explicit colon + line break + value on the next line is shown as label, colon, same line break and one marker; no character of the value visible.
requirements.note: `_separator_end` and `_skip_gap` now skip whitespace including line breaks, while only the value span is replaced, so the separator and line break stay. Covered by the new colon/equals line-break tests and the acceptance check that passed.

requirements.requirement: FR-2 / AC-2 / AC-3: the line-break rule works both for one block of text and for separate display lines, keeps the line count and leaves all other lines character for character.
requirements.note: Masking operates on the whole text and the gap/separator skips only whitespace, so no newline is consumed or added; unit tests assert the line count and unchanged neighbouring lines, and the session test asserts the masked reply lines.

requirements.requirement: FR-3 / AC-4: a punctuation-prefixed value after ':' or '=' is masked together with its leading punctuation, with the label, separator and space visible and exactly one marker.
requirements.note: `_explicit_span`/`_marked_span` replace the punctuation and the value with one marker for any punctuation, not only the examples in the finding; covered for '!', '@', '#' across several labels.

requirements.requirement: FR-4 / AC-5: a bracketed value after an explicit separator is masked entirely, brackets included, with exactly one marker.
requirements.note: `_VALUE_BRACKETS` handles the bracketed run whole, so no bracket or value character survives; tests cover '[hunter2]', '[abc123]' and a spaced bracketed value.

requirements.requirement: FR-5 / AC-6: quoted values keep their current rendering, quotes visible with the marker between them.
requirements.note: `_explicit_span` sends quote pairs to the unchanged `_span` path; the existing quoted-value expectations still pass.

requirements.requirement: FR-6: repeated separator characters stay visible and only the value is replaced.
requirements.note: Only the value span is replaced; the separator run including repeats and interleaved whitespace is untouched, matching the existing repeated-separator expectations and the new '==' case.

requirements.requirement: FR-7 / AC-10: exactly one marker per masked value and masking twice equals masking once, including the new forms.
requirements.note: `_explicit_span` recognises the existing marker first, and bracket/word spans never re-include it; the dedicated idempotence test asserts one marker and a fixed point for every new form.

requirements.requirement: FR-8: no character of a masked value appears anywhere in the shown text for every new and existing form.
requirements.note: The whole span is replaced in one substitution; tests assert the secret is absent and the marker count is one.

requirements.requirement: FR-9 / AC-7 / AC-8: a label mention without a value (same line or followed by a line break) and an authorization scheme before a credential keep today's rendering.
requirements.note:
The separator/punctuation path returns None when no value follows, existing mention/function-word/narrative-word exceptions and the auth-scheme pass-through are preserved, and tests cover 'password:', 'password:
', 'password:

' and the bearer form.

requirements.requirement: FR-10 / AC-9: secret-free text, including punctuation, line breaks and several lines, is returned unchanged character for character.
requirements.note: Non-secret labels never enter the binding path and the masking replaces only spans; tests cover multiline secret-free text in English and Russian and the full existing suite still passes per QA.

requirements.requirement: FR-11 / AC-11: every masking form the client already handles keeps its current rendering and the whole existing expectation suite passes.
requirements.note: No existing expectation was removed or weakened; the environment gate and test runs passed and the preserved space/colon/equals/quote/JSON/quoted-label cases are untouched.

requirements.requirement: AC-12 (review-only): the finding is resolved for any secret label, any explicit separator and any punctuation, not only the named examples.
requirements.note: The rule is generic over labels (including Russian stems, compounds and quoted labels), both explicit separators and any non-alphanumeric punctuation; tests exercise several labels, separators and punctuation characters, so the fix is not tuned to the audit examples.

requirements.requirement: Scope and repository rules: one coherent change, only needed files, no unrelated/temporary/debug/generated files, no unrequested feature, no weakened or deleted test, no documentation change.
requirements.note: Only `forgel_code/interactive.py` and `tests/test_redact.py` are committed; the added test engine is a legitimate test fixture, there is no configuration, interface or documentation change, and no test removal was detected.
